title: 24. Teenage Break-Up Protocol: How to Figure Out if You Need to End a Relationships, the 8-Step Approach to Ending it, and Break-Up Horror Stories!
description_html:
In this episode, Steph and I sit down to go through break-up protocol! Like we mentioned in today's episode, we're not experts, just speaking from experience and hoping to help. If you're in a relationship that feels unsafe, please talk to an adult you trust! 

“A break-up is an opportunity to learn, too. It's not easy. But it's a chance to do your best to respect another person's feelings. Ending a relationship — as hard as it is — builds our skills when it comes to being honest and kind during difficult conversations.” - https://kidshealth.org/ConnecticutChildrens/en/teens/break-up.html#
talk_about: Tell your SO you have something important to talk about with them
Start by saying something you appreciate about the other person
Explain the primary reason why you believe that you should break up
Say, very clearly, that you want to break up.
Say something positive while not being invalidating
Listen to what they have to say
summary: sadie and her friend stephanie walk through breakup protocol for teen relationships. they cover red flags to watch for (lack of trust, friends/family not liking your partner, feeling insecure), reasons you might need to end things (no longer attracted, arguing more than having fun, wanting different levels of commitment), and an 8-step approach to breaking up respectfully. they emphasize doing it in person (never over text if you're official), choosing a neutral/private space, being clear and kind, and giving the other person space afterward. sadie shares her own breakup horror stories to illustrate what not to do—like telling friends before your partner, or breaking up right before a family dinner.
